memos.headline: Momentum Bifurcation: S07/S09 at New Highs While S04/S03/S02 Break Down Hard
memos.body: I see a sharply divided tape today. On the strong side, S07 and S09 are both sitting at 52-week highs with 26-week returns of +69% and +36% respectively, though RSIs of 71 and 78 warn of near-term overextension—S09 in particular trades 19% above its 50-day mean, which historically invites a pullback. S08 and S01 look cleaner with strong uptrends, moderate RSIs (69 and 75), and solid relative strength versus SPY. On the weak side, S04 (RSI 29, -26% from highs), S03 (RSI 29, -17% from highs), and S02 (RSI 33, an extraordinary -54% drawdown from 52-week highs) are in full breakdown mode with deeply negative relative strength. I would lean into the S08 trend and wait for S09/S07 to consolidate before adding, while avoiding the broken names until they reclaim their 50-day averages.

views.note: Clean uptrend: +7.4% over 4w, +3.5% above 50d, RSI 69 not yet overbought, only -2.8% from highs; would reassess on a close below the 50-day mean (~269).
Strong 4w +12.5% rally with positive relative strength vs SPY (+12.3% over 4w), low ATR of 1.76% suggests orderly advance; risk is RSI 75 signals short-term stretch, would cut below 50d mean (~146).
At 52-week highs with massive +69% 26w gain and 18% above 50d mean—trend is undeniable but extension is extreme; waiting for a pullback toward the 50d (~615) before getting involved.
New highs and dominant relative strength (+21% vs SPY over 4w), but RSI 77.6 and 19% above 50d mean screams near-term exhaustion; would buy a retest of ~130-135 area.
Steady but uninspiring: only -3.6% from highs, RSI 59, but 4w relative strength vs SPY is -2.4%—not broken but not leading either.
Massive 26w gain of +70.7% but now consolidating near 50d mean with RSI 44.7 and slight negative 4w relative strength; needs to hold ~320 or risk a deeper correction.
In freefall: -16.1% over 4w, RSI 29, -14.4% below 50d mean, -22.1% relative strength vs SPY over 12w—classic broken trend, would reconsider only on a sustained close above the 50d mean (~469).
RSI 28.6 with -14.6% over 4w and -16.7% relative underperformance vs SPY over 12w; catching this knife requires a reclaim of the 200d mean (~223).
The worst chart in the universe: -53.9% drawdown from 52w high, -20.2% over 4w, RSI 33, ATR nearly 5%—no reason to step in front of this until it stabilizes above the 50d mean (~326).
Middling: RSI 51, flat 4w return, -8.2% relative underperformance vs SPY over 12w—no edge either way, watching for a break above or below the 50d mean (~184).

memos.headline: S10 and S04 Lead on Earnings Power; S02 and S09 Flash Margin Compression Warnings
memos.body: I see a clear bifurcation in this universe between durable high-margin growers and names suffering earnings erosion. S10 stands out with 56% net margins, +62.5% YoY revenue growth, and minimal debt ($8.47B), making it the strongest fundamental profile in the group. S04 is close behind at 47.3% net margins with net income surging +59.5% YoY on $81.27B of revenue. On the other end, S02 posted a 2.1% net margin with net income collapsing -61.2% YoY despite +12.2% revenue growth—classic cash-flow compression I refuse to pay for. S09 is also deteriorating with revenue declining -5.2% and net income down -12.3%, leaving an 8.8% margin on $32.82B of debt. I would need to see margin stabilization in S02 and S09 before reconsidering; for S10 and S04, any deceleration in revenue growth or margin contraction would change my view.

views.note: 56% net margin, +62.5% revenue growth, and only $8.47B debt represent the best earnings quality in the universe.
47.3% net margin with +59.5% YoY net income growth and manageable $40.26B debt signal durable earnings power.
30.3% net margin, +18% revenue growth, +29.8% net income growth, and low $14.79B debt make this a clean compounder.
$143.76B revenue growing +15.7% with 29.3% margins is solid, though $88.50B total debt warrants monitoring.
Revenue of $180.17B growing +13.4% is impressive but 11.8% net margin leaves limited cushion; need to see margin expansion.
31% net margin is healthy but $427.2B total debt dwarfs peers and +8.8% revenue growth is the slowest among profitable names.
19.4% margin is decent but +1.5% revenue growth and -6.7% net income decline suggest stalling momentum.
13% margin and +9.5% revenue growth are acceptable but -6.7% net income decline and $31.74B debt on $17.64B revenue give me pause.
Revenue declining -5.2% with net income down -12.3% and an 8.8% margin on $32.82B debt signals deteriorating earnings power.
Net income collapsed -61.2% YoY to a razor-thin 2.1% margin despite +12.2% revenue growth—textbook cash-flow compression.

memos.headline: Fed Easing Cycle Intact but Sticky CPI and Rising Long Rates Argue for Quality Over Pure Duration Bets
memos.body: I see the Fed firmly in an easing regime: the upper bound has fallen 75 bp over the past year to 3.75%, with the effective rate at 3.64%, and the curve has re-steepened sharply (10y-2y spread +48 bp YoY to 0.74 pp). However, CPI is running at 2.7% YoY and the 3-month annualized pace (~2.4%) suggests disinflation is stalling, which could slow further cuts. Unemployment at 4.4% is up 30 bp YoY but flat over three months, consistent with a soft-landing rather than outright recession. The 10y yield has actually risen 11 bp over three months to 4.22%, signaling the long end is repricing term premium or growth expectations higher. A CPI print above 3% or unemployment jumping above 4.6% would materially change my regime call; absent that, I expect a prolonged pause after one more cut, favoring sectors that benefit from a steeper curve and moderate growth over pure duration plays.

views.note: Banks benefit directly from a steeper yield curve (+48 bp YoY in 10y-2y spread) and continued moderate growth backdrop.
Cyclicals are supported by a soft-landing labor market (unemployment flat at 4.4% over 3m) and easing financial conditions.
Duration-sensitive growth gets a tailwind from lower front-end rates but the 11 bp rise in the 10y over 3 months caps upside.
Staples offer defensive value but the macro regime is not recessionary enough to warrant an overweight; CPI at 2.7% pressures margins.
Energy benefits from moderate nominal growth and sticky inflation; real rates are declining as the Fed eases, supporting commodity demand.
Long-duration rate-sensitive names face headwinds from the 10y yield grinding higher over the past quarter despite Fed cuts.

memos.headline: Post-Earnings Sentiment Divergence: S02 and S04 Crushed, S07 and S01 Quietly Positive
memos.body: I am reading the earnings-season price reactions across the universe as the primary sentiment signal this cycle. S02 dropped -19.6% on its Jan-27 results and S04 fell -10.0% on Jan-28, indicating severely negative narrative shifts that likely have not fully cleared given the magnitude. S03 just printed -5.6% on Feb-05/06, suggesting fresh negative sentiment still being digested. On the positive side, S07 gained +3.4% on Jan-29 results and S01 rose +2.6% on Jan-22 earnings, both modest but constructive moves that suggest sentiment is turning up without being crowded. S08 and S09 had muted reactions (+0.5% and +0.6% respectively), which I read as neutral—no narrative shift either way.

views.note: Positive +3.4% earnings reaction with governance changes earlier in Jan suggests constructive narrative building without crowded optimism.
Solid +2.6% earnings reaction on Jan-22 and active Reg FD disclosures signal improving tone with room to run.
A -19.6% earnings-day collapse on Jan-27 signals a severe negative narrative shift that is unlikely to reverse quickly.
The -10.0% post-earnings drop on Jan-28 reflects a sharp negative sentiment break; I see no catalyst for near-term recovery.
Fresh -5.6% reaction on Feb-05/06 earnings means negative sentiment is still being absorbed as of today.
Heavy filing activity including a -4.2% earnings reaction in mid-Jan, director changes, and multiple Other Events filings create a noisy, unclear sentiment picture.
Muted +0.5% earnings reaction and a director change filing suggest no meaningful sentiment shift in either direction.
Flat +0.6% earnings reaction on Jan-30 indicates the market is indifferent; no narrative to trade here.
Negligible -0.5% earnings reaction on Feb-04 suggests sentiment is balanced with no strong directional signal.
Only a director change filing with no earnings data available; insufficient information to form a sentiment view.

memos.headline: VIX Spike and Rising Oil Signal Elevated Geopolitical Risk; Policy Uncertainty Easing but Volatility Persists
memos.body: I note a sharp 46% one-month surge in the VIX to 21.77 alongside an 8.3% monthly jump in WTI crude to $62.90, suggesting markets are pricing in geopolitical or policy-driven supply disruption risk. The economic policy uncertainty index at 291.35 has actually fallen 46% over the past month, which I read as a resolution of a specific policy shock (possibly tariff or sanctions-related) rather than a structural de-risking. High-yield OAS widened modestly by 16bp month-over-month to 2.97%, consistent with a risk-off tilt that has not yet reached stress levels. The 10y-2y spread steepening to +0.74pp over three months suggests the market is repricing term premium, possibly reflecting fiscal or energy-security concerns. Without explicit GDELT event data on sanctions or export controls, I am relying on macro proxies and 8-K filings, which limits my conviction on company-specific geopolitical exposure.

views.note: Three 8-K filings in under a month (including two 8.01 Other Events) suggest active corporate developments, but without content detail I cannot determine geopolitical exposure direction.
Two Reg FD filings in January signal management communication but no clear geopolitical catalyst; holding neutral pending clarity on supply-chain or China-policy exposure.
Back-to-back Reg FD disclosures in January could reflect guidance updates amid policy uncertainty, but the declining EPU index suggests the worst may have passed for policy-sensitive names.
Single Reg FD filing on Jan 29 provides no actionable geopolitical signal; VIX spike warrants caution but no directional call without more data.
With WTI up 8.3% m/m and VIX surging 46%, names with energy-cost sensitivity or supply-chain concentration risk face headwinds; I lean avoid on S05 absent evidence of hedging or diversification.
One Reg FD filing in mid-January and no further disclosures; macro backdrop is mixed with easing policy uncertainty but rising vol, so I stay neutral.
